# GSC Search Analytics API

The GSC API has one primary endpoint — `searchanalytics.query.` 

Must understand the dimension system: the same endpoint returns different views by changing `dimensions`, `dimensionFilterGroups`, and `rowLimit`.

| // Base request structure \-- all Search Analytics calls share this shapePOST https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites/{siteUrl}/searchAnalytics/query{  "startDate": "2025-01-01",  "endDate": "2025-03-31",  "dimensions": \[\],            // controls what the rows represent  "dimensionFilterGroups": \[\], // filters rows by dimension values  "rowLimit": 5000,            // max 25000; paginate via startRow  "startRow": 0,  "dataState": "final"         // or "all" for fresher but incomplete data} |
| :---- |

![][image1]

# **Usage Limits**

## **QPS quota**

The Search Analytics resource enforces the following QPS (queries per second) QPM (queries per minute) and QPD (queries per day) limits:

    Per-site quota (calls querying the same site):  
        1,200 QPM  
    Per-user quota (calls made by the same user):  
        1,200 QPM   
    Per-project quota (calls made using the same Developer Console key):  
        30,000,000 QPD  
        40,000 QPM

Example

    User A can make up to 1,200 QPM combined to her 3 websites.  
    Users A and B can make up to 1,200 QPM combined to their one website.

## **URL inspection**

    index inspection quota  
    Per-site quota (calls querying the same site):  
        2000 QPD  
        600 QPM  
    Per-project quota (calls made using the same Developer Console key):  
        10,000,000 QPD  
        15,000 QPM

## **All other resources**

    Per-user limit (calls made by the same user):  
        20 QPS  
        200 QPM  
    Per-project limit (calls made using the same Developer Console key):  
        100,000,000 QPD

1. **Top Keywords for Site**

| {  dimensions: \["query"\],  rowLimit: 5000}// Returns: one row per keyword across the whole site// Fields per row: keys\[0\] \= keyword, clicks, impressions, ctr, position// Sort by: impressions DESC for prompt enrichment; clicks DESC for revenue signal |
| :---- |

   

2. **Top Pages for Site**

| {  dimensions: \["page"\],  rowLimit: 5000}// Returns: one row per landing page// Fields per row: keys\[0\] \= full page URL, clicks, impressions, ctr, position// Use: identify which pages have strong search presence but no AI visibility |
| :---- |

   

   

3. **Top Keywords for a Specific Page**

| {  dimensions: \["query"\],  dimensionFilterGroups: \[{    filters: \[{      dimension: "page",      operator: "equals",      expression: "https://example.com/pricing"    }\]  }\],  rowLimit: 5000}// Returns: all keywords driving traffic to that page// Use: reverse-engineer what topics a page owns vs. what it could own in AI |
| :---- |

   

4. **Top Pages for a Keyword**

| {  dimensions: \["page"\],  dimensionFilterGroups: \[{    filters: \[{      dimension: "query",      operator: "equals",  // or "contains" for broader matching      expression: "crm for startups"    }\]  }\],  rowLimit: 100}// Returns: which pages rank for this keyword, with their individual metrics// Use: when scoring a gap, identify which existing page would win the citation |
| :---- |

   

5. **Page-Keyword Breakdown (pages with their keywords)**

| {  dimensions: \["page", "query"\],  // order matters: page is the primary grouping  rowLimit: 25000}// Returns: one row per (page, keyword) pair// This is the most expensive call \-- always paginate and cache aggressively// Use: build the full keyword-to\-page ownership map for gap classification |
| :---- |

   

   

6. **Keyword-Page Breakdown (keywords with their pages)**

| {  dimensions: \["query", "page"\],  // order reversed from above  rowLimit: 25000}// Returns: one row per (keyword, page) pair, grouped by keyword// Same data as \#5, different sort order \-- both can be derived from one call// Recommendation: run \#5 once, store the joint table, query it both ways |
| :---- |

   

7.  **Page Performance Over Time**

| {  dimensions: \["date", "page"\],  // date dimension unlocks time series  dimensionFilterGroups: \[{    filters: \[{      dimension: "page",      operator: "equals",      expression: "https://example.com/blog/what-is-crm"    }\]  }\],  rowLimit: 90  // one row per day across 90-day window}// Returns: daily performance trend for a specific page// Use: detect content decay \-- a page losing position signals staleness refresh needed |
| :---- |

   

8. **Check Indexing Status (separate API)**

| // This is the URL Inspection API, not Search AnalyticsPOST https://searchconsole.googleapis.com/v1/urlInspectionResult:inspect{  "inspectionUrl": "https://example.com/blog/what-is-crm",  "siteUrl": "https://example.com/"}// Returns:{  "indexStatusResult": {    "verdict": "PASS" | "NEUTRAL" | "FAIL",    "coverageState": "Submitted and indexed",    "indexingState": "INDEXING\_ALLOWED",    "lastCrawlTime": "2025-04-10T14:22:00Z",    "pageFetchState": "SUCCESSFUL",    "robotsTxtState": "ALLOWED",    "crawledAs": "DESKTOP"  }}// Critical for Gravton: a page with high-impression keywords but FAIL verdict// is a technical gap, not a content gap \-- routes to technical agent, not content agent |
| :---- |
